author: Josh DuBose
title: Fiery West L.A. pursuit crash leaves several people seriously injured - NewsBreak
text: A stolen vehicle suspect who was leading deputies with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department in pursuit while tossing car batteries from the window caused a fiery multi-vehicle crash that injured five people Wednesday evening. The wanted driver was leading deputies in chase in the westbound lanes of the 10 Freeway when they reportedly started tossing out car batteries, adding assault with a deadly weapon to the potential charges they could face. It’s currently unclear exactly how the crash occurred, but preliminary information suggests that at least three vehicles were involved in the collision, one of which burst into flames. It’s unknown if any of those involved in the pursuit crash were trapped in their vehicles, but officials said four people suffered serious injuries and were rushed to the hospital in unknown conditions. A fifth person suffered minor injuries and was being evaluated at the scene, officials told KTLA. Among the injured were two suspects, who were taken into custody and transported to the hospital, officials with the sheriff’s department told KTLA. Aerial footage captured by Sky showed a heavy presence of law enforcement and firefighters at the 10 Freeway crash site, near Overland Avenue and National Boulevard. Fire crews were seen spraying water on a smoldering vehicle, while medical personnel attended to several of those injured on the side of the freeway. So far, there have been no reports that any deputies were injured during the pursuit. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to KTLA.
